title: Code edit obeys project rule: no secret values in wrangler vars

claim.statement: The candidate's edit to wrangler configuration adds no secret value (API key, token, password, or private key) under `vars`; secrets are referenced only through Worker secrets, per the project rule used by abide.

question.instructions: The state is one unified diff hunk from a code edit plus its file path. Project rule: a wrangler configuration must never place a secret value (API key, token, password, private key, or credential string) under `vars`; secrets are declared as Worker secrets and referenced by name only. Which option describes the added lines of this edit?

criteria.A: the added lines comply with the rule
criteria.B: the added lines put a secret value under vars, violating the rule
criteria.C: the edit does not touch wrangler vars, so the rule does not apply

notes: UNMEASURED: no TypeSafe Jev API credentials were available when the Laya rubrics were calibrated (docs/calibration/system1-calibration-report.md), so this rubric has no calibration set, no fitted temperature, no control fixtures, and no replay measurement. The all-zero calibration_set_digest and control input_digest values are placeholders, temperature 1 is not fitted, and calibration_set_size and measured_ece are not measurements. assurance_eligible is false until a calibration run on Jev replaces them (a new rubric_version and a plan amendment).

Jev is hosted and closed: the pinned model_version is the only revision handle, fresh-process replay is not available, and a served version other than 1.13.0 is ERROR `model_revision_mismatch`. That is why epsilon is wider (0.01) than for pinned CPU Laya.

Published third-party Jev ECE figures (as returned) range from 0.144 (typed-decisions) to 0.246; measured_ece 0.144 is that published figure, not a measurement on this rubric. It was not measured on this rubric.
Neutral option keys (A/B/C) with the verdict in the description avoid label-following on yes/no wording.
The input budget uses UTF-8 bytes as a conservative token bound because Jev's tokenizer is not available client-side; 4000 is a chosen budget, not Jev's documented context limit.
This is a rule-conformance verdict on a fixed diff, not code review: Jev never proposes a fix, rewrites the diff, or judges code quality.
